source.title: Decomposing the QK circuit with Bilinear Sparse Dictionary Learning

page_placements.theme: Sparse and low-rank channels within attention
Dictionary geometry, stability and utilization depend on training

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse dictionary learning to QK activations in GPT2-small and reports recovered features and attention-pattern reconstruction, extending dictionary-feature evidence to a new model component.
record.gate_note: The study does not test toy-model superposition or measure feature-direction geometry, interference, or a sparsity-dependent transition. Rows record its own GPT2-small dictionary-feature and reconstruction results. Numeric values visible only in the attention-reconstruction figures are not available in the text.
record.test_reason: The study uses sparse dictionary learning as a tool to decompose GPT2-small's QK circuit and mainly reports its own method's performance: L0, mask sparsity and attention-pattern reconstruction. Its transcoders are trained to reconstruct attention patterns, not activations. So its sparsity, live-feature and density results do not measure whether the model's activations contain SAE-recoverable sparse features (V4). It tests no geometry, capacity, polysemanticity, canonicity or dimensionality claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors also suggest that much residual-stream variance is attention-irrelevant and that very few feature pairs matter for pattern reconstruction. They note dense features, including an 'attend to BOS' flag, and that 80-95% of features die.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse query/key encoder-decoders and a learned feature-pair mask to reconstruct GPT2-small attention patterns; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments or measure their feature-direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The live-feature counts vary by layer and between query and key dictionaries. The study does not report a systematic comparison of the main reconstruction finding across settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Transcoders trained to reconstruct attention patterns keep only 144-524 of 2400 features live (80-95% die). This is robust across hyperparameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: QK circuits in GPT2-small use a small set of residual-stream features, relative to residual-stream SAE feature counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Query/key transcoder features are on average significantly denser than residual-stream SAE features. One dense query feature acts as an 'attend to BOS' flag.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention-relevant features may be dense rather than sparse, contrary to the sparsity assumption of SDL.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention patterns are accurately reconstructed from small dictionaries, and >99.9% of query-key feature pairs can be masked.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Much residual-stream variance is irrelevant to a given layer's attention pattern.

record.problems: The authors characterize the applications as preliminary and likely suboptimally trained, report opaque features and dead features, and have not tested other models with enough confidence to assess scaling. Numerical values for the pattern-reconstruction figures are not given in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for Figs. 3-6 because numerical values are not stated and the text gives only an aggregate reconstruction description (captured in r11). Comparisons or observations cited from other work were not recorded as study results.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
It does not measure feature spread across neurons, or SAE recovery of activations; the dictionaries are trained on attention-pattern loss.
It does not test completeness, stability or canonicity of dictionary features.
It does not compare 1-D with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper (an Alignment Forum post). Its dictionaries reconstruct attention patterns, not activations, so its results are about the method and about QK feature usage rather than the superposition claim versions. The reader's V4 support/limits labels are removed. Comments mention that an L2-targeted SAE needed d_hidden around 16,000 for comparable pattern reconstruction; this is an author comment, not a reported result.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, geometry, and a sparsity-dependent transition.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Does not test feature spread across neurons in the residual stream generally, or compare recovered features across models. Tests dictionary recovery for QK-related features in GPT2-small.
Does not test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses feature directions in its representation, but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

relation.reason: Uses sparse feature dictionaries as an interpretability tool without directly testing the listed claim versions.

tranche.reason: Uses sparse dictionary learning to decompose attention and reports its own reconstruction, sparsity and interpretability results. Investigating superposition among heads is proposed as future work.

source_check.notes: The authors acknowledge likely suboptimal training and no neuron resampling. The >99.9% masking figure includes dead features; conditioning on live features gives 80–90% sparsity.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small QK dictionaries at layers 2, 6, and 10
reader_labels.reason: The learned dictionaries have reported sparse L0 and support accurate attention-pattern reconstruction; the study also reports live features at each layer (r1-r8, r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Both dictionaries' activations are reported as significantly denser on average than residual-stream SAEs for the same layers, qualifying how sparse these recovered features are (r9-r10).
